name: Massachusetts

statute.readVia: https://web.archive.org/web/20260517121552/https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXIV/Chapter90/Section9D (archived copy of the official page dated 2026-05-17; malegislature.gov refused our connection)

statute.cite: 540 CMR 4.04(8)(g) window tinting inspection standard (Mass Vehicle Check station guideline)

windshield.strip: any transparent material limited to the uppermost 6 inches along the top of the windshield, not encroaching on the driver's direct forward viewing area (FMVSS); inspection guideline: not lower than 6 in. from the top or lower than the AS1 marks
windshield.reflective: statute allows only 'transparent material' on the top strip; inspection guideline bars tinting or reflective material lower than 6 in./AS1

rear.note: rear window tint requires two outside mirrors, one on each side

tint.measuredHow: film + glass combined (RMV inspection: meter reading 'will transmit through both the window and the tint film')

reflectivity.front: total visible light reflectance not more than 35%
reflectivity.back: total visible light reflectance not more than 35%

tint.dualMirrors: Required for tinted rear window (and for draperies/louvers on rear or rear side windows): two outside mirrors, one on each side.
tint.certificateOrSticker: Medical exemption: the Registrar issues a noticeable sticker affixed to the side window immediately adjacent to the operator.

medicalExemption.text: For a light- or photosensitive owner or operator of a private passenger vehicle: written application to the RMV Medical Advisory Board, supported by a written attestation from a physician licensed in Massachusetts; if granted, the Registrar issues a sticker for the driver's side window (RMV Tinted Glass Medical Waiver form).

penalty.text: Fine of not more than $250; on a third or subsequent conviction the Registrar suspends the licence for up to 90 days; vehicle also fails the annual safety inspection

quotes: § 9D(4): "nontransparent or sunscreen material or window application which has a total visible light reflectance of not more than thirty-five per cent or a visible light transmittance of not less than thirty-five per cent on the side windows"
§ 9D(4) cont.: "the side windows immediately to the rear of the operator's seat and the front passenger seat or on the rear window if the vehicle is equipped with two outside mirrors"
§ 9D(5): "the use of any transparent material limited to the uppermost 6″ along the top of the windshield"
§ 9D: "Violations of any provisions of this section shall be punishable by a fine of not more than two hundred and fifty dollars."

RMV/Mass Vehicle Check guideline: "reads less than 35% light transmittance. The percentage number that the meter reports indicates the amount of light that will transmit through both the window and the tint film"

helmet.conditions: every operator and passenger (incl. sidecar); eye protection if no windshield

handheldPhone.noviceOrAgeBan: Junior operators (under 18) may not use any mobile electronic device, even hands-free (ch. 90 § 8M) - not re-read in official text
handheldPhone.fineText: first offense $100, second $250, third or subsequent $500; second+ offense also requires a registrar-selected program

radarDetector.note: No Massachusetts ban on radar detectors in passenger vehicles found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

openQuestions: malegislature.gov refused connections on 2026-10-24; § 9D read on the archived copy of the official page of 2026-05-17, § 7 on that of 2026-08-11, § 13B on that of 2026-10-16.
Reflectance: statute says 'reflectance of not more than 35% OR transmittance of not less than 35%' - ambiguous 'or'; RMV inspection applies the 35% transmittance test.
No tolerance found; no colour restriction found in § 9D.
Studded tires: secondary sources give Nov 1 (or Nov 2) - Apr 30, cite disputed (ch. 90 § 16 or registrar rule); not confirmed in an official text, left null.
Underglow and lift/height limits (540 CMR 4.00 inspection rules) not found; left null.
Junior operator ban (§ 8M) and primary-enforcement status not read in the official text.
